Strategy Performance Review¶

What this is: an end-to-end review of every order placed in the Alpaca paper account since trading began (Feb 2026 → Apr 2026 — roughly the last ~3 months).

Where the data comes from: data/orders_latest.csv, exported by the Close Report GitHub Action (the same src/report.py that runs every trading day). One row per order, FIFO-matched realized PnL on the SELL side.

How orders are tagged: the bot stamps every algorithmic order with client_order_id = \"{strategy_id}:{uuid}\". Anything without that prefix is a manual order placed from the Alpaca dashboard — labeled here as Discretionary.

The four buckets:

Bucket Source Lifetime budget
Clenow Trend strategies.momentum.clenow_trend \$5,000
Ranked Asset Allocation V10 strategies.ranks.ranked_asset_alloc \$15,000
High Pullback Reversion strategies.mean_reversion.high_pullback_reversion \$10,000
Discretionary manual orders from the Alpaca dashboard n/a

The rest of the notebook walks through capital deployment, realized PnL, trade cadence, concentration, and a side-by-side comparison.

1. Load and tag the order tape¶

The CSV already carries Strategy Type / Strategy Name columns parsed from client_order_id. Anything that wasn't generated by one of our three strategies (i.e. blank Strategy Name) is reclassified as Discretionary. We also keep only filled orders — anything else never moved cash.

2. Headline scoreboard¶

For each bucket we collapse all of its filled orders into a single row of summary stats:

  • Bought — total dollars deployed on BUY fills
  • Sold — total dollars recovered on SELL fills
  • Net Deployed — Bought − Sold (capital still tied up in open positions, ignoring mark-to-market)
  • Realized PnL — sum of FIFO-matched PnL on SELL fills
  • Round-trip Win Rate — share of closed (matched) SELLs that ended green
  • Budget Used — Net Deployed / Lifetime Budget for the three algorithmic strategies

3. Where the cash actually went¶

The bar on the left shows total dollars deployed (BUY fills) per bucket, with a horizontal "lifetime budget" line for each algorithmic strategy. Discretionary trading dwarfs the algos in raw dollar terms — that's the headline finding of this section.

The right panel shows realized PnL: dollars actually pocketed (or lost) on closed round-trips. Open positions are excluded — they don't show up here until they're sold.

4. Budget gauges (algorithmic strategies only)¶

For each algo strategy, how much of its lifetime budget is currently sitting in open positions versus available to redeploy. Sell proceeds recycle back into the budget — this picture changes daily as positions roll.

5. Net deployed capital over time¶

Cumulative BUY − SELL per bucket. A rising line means capital is going in; a falling line means positions are being closed and cash is coming back. Discretionary trades show big lumps where a manual basket of names was bought all at once.

6. Cumulative realized PnL¶

Each line steps up (or down) every time a position is closed. This excludes unrealized PnL on positions still held.

7. Per-trade PnL distribution¶

Strip plot: every closed round-trip is one dot. Y-axis is dollars made or lost on that single trade. Useful for spotting fat tails (one big loser dragging an otherwise-fine strategy down).

8. Activity heatmap — when does each bucket trade?¶

Number of orders per (week, bucket). Confirms that the algos run in tight clusters on their scheduled days, while discretionary activity is bursty.

9. Best and worst trades¶

Top 8 winners and top 8 losers across everything. Each bar is colored by the bucket that owned the trade — useful for confirming whether one bucket is over-represented in the tails.

10. Symbol concentration¶

Treemap-style view of the top 20 symbols by total dollars bought. Box size = dollars deployed; color = the bucket that owned it. Big red boxes are large discretionary single-name bets.

11. Strategy DNA — average ticket size and cadence¶

Two complementary lenses on how each bucket trades, independent of how much money it makes:

  • Avg ticket size = average dollars per BUY fill — how concentrated each entry is
  • Trades per active week = order count divided by the number of distinct calendar weeks the bucket was active

One compact figure that puts all four buckets next to each other on the dimensions that matter — gross dollars in, dollars out, net still deployed, and realized PnL. The visual answer to "which strategy did what".

14. Auto-generated narrative¶

A short paragraph that re-derives itself from the numbers above so it stays in sync next time the report is refreshed.

Window: Feb 02, 2026 – Apr 17, 2026 (74 days)¶

  • Gross dollars deployed across all buckets: $108.2k; recovered through SELL fills: $59.5k.
  • Realized PnL (closed round-trips only): $3.4k.
  • Discretionary share of gross deployment: 77% — manual orders are the dominant capital flow, by a wide margin.

By bucket:

  • Clenow Trend — bought $11.3k, currently net-deployed $6.0k, using 121% of the $5.0k lifetime budget (room for -$1.0k more); realized PnL -$469, win rate 36% on 14 closed trades.
  • Ranked Asset Alloc — bought $13.4k, currently net-deployed $8.0k, using 53% of the $15.0k lifetime budget (room for $7.0k more); realized PnL -$256, win rate 0% on 3 closed trades.
  • Discretionary — bought $83.5k, currently net-deployed $34.7k; realized PnL $4.1k, win rate 100% on 14 closed trades.

Best single trade so far: UNH on Apr 16, $1.8k (Discretionary). Worst single trade so far: XLC on Apr 01, -$171 (Ranked Asset Alloc). Best bucket on realized PnL: Discretionary ($4.1k). **Worst bucket on realized PnL:** Clenow Trend (-$469).

How to refresh¶

The latest order tape lives in data/orders_latest.csv. To pull a fresh copy from the live paper account:

gh run download $(gh run list -R Shazil10/alpaca-paper-trader --workflow "Close Report" --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId') \
  -R Shazil10/alpaca-paper-trader \
  --dir /tmp/latest && \
cp /tmp/latest/trading-reports-close/orders_latest.csv Assignment_final/data/orders_latest.csv

Then "Restart & Run All" in the notebook. Every chart, every metric, every paragraph re-derives from the CSV — nothing is hard-coded.
